subject: Inference affordability recap, constraints, and proposed pilot next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@cardinalpay.com>
Cc: platform@cardinalpay.com
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap from today — affordability constraints & proposed pilot

Thanks again for taking the call today, Elena — appreciate the candid conversation. Below is a short recap so we’re aligned and to make the next steps explicit.

High-level conclusion
- CardinalPay is interested in a narrow pilot to validate inference quality and cost assumptions, but budget is constrained (~$10k–$15k/month allocation for the first 60 days).

Pain points you shared
- Current vendor costs are unpredictable at scale (token-driven spend) and are outpacing product economics for low-value transactional flows.
- Tight SLOs: median request latency target ~200–300ms P95 for end-user flows.
- Data governance: some records have PII and need retention/access controls.

Goals for pilot
- Demonstrate a predictable cost curve and unit economics for the high-volume transaction path (card auth messaging + contextual account info).
- Show latency within your SLOs while using batching/caching levers to reduce unit cost.
- Validate integration with your VPC/KMS requirements (if pilot moves to private).

Cost/TCO assumptions we discussed (rough initial estimates)
- Example transaction average: ~400 prompt tokens + 150 completion tokens = ~550 tokens per interaction (we used your sample payloads).
- If we run at 200k interactions/month => ~110M tokens/month.
- With continuous batching and prefix KV caching we expect token savings in the ~20–35% range for this workload shape (depends on cache hit rate and prompt similarity).
- Targeted pilot pricing: aiming to get to an effective $/1k-token near your target budget — we modeled several levers in the attached pilot_budget.xlsx.

Levers to reduce spend (we’ll instrument these during pilot)
- Continuous batching (worker-side scheduling) to increase throughput and lower per-token overhead.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated contextual elements to drop prompt tokens.
- Lower-precision model variants (INT8/quantized) for background/low-sensitivity requests.
- Rate-based routing: route to cheaper model variants for non-critical paths.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm the rough budget band you can commit for the 6–8 week pilot (you mentioned $10–15k/mo)?
2) Would an NDA/Security questionnaire and SOC2 evidence be required before we run a small sandbox? We can provide a short security snippet now (low-level items are attached) and SOC2 evidence link.
3) Proposed schedule: kickoff next Wed 10:00 AM PT for a 30–45m technical alignment (integration points + sample dataset).

Attachments: CardinalPay_pilot_budget.xlsx (cost model + sample scenarios)

If that all looks right I’ll follow up with a one-page SOW and calendar invite for Wed.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Thanks Rachel — clear recap, appreciate the math. A few quick clarifications:

- Budget: we can likely commit up to $12k/month initially but need procurement sign-off.

- Security: SOC2 is required for production; for a sandbox we need minimal controls in place (VPC peering or isolated project, retention limited to 30 days). Can you attach your SOC2 summary and a short note on retention/keys?

Let’s tentatively hold Wed 10am PT for the technical kickoff. I’ll confirm after I sync with finance.

—Elena

Great — thanks for the quick reply, Elena. A few notes to help when you look at the sample payloads:

Token estimate basis
- The ~550-token example came from the sample transaction we reviewed: 8 lines of contextual account metadata (~250 tokens) + user prompt (~150 tokens) + expected assistant reasoning/completion (~150 tokens). If your sample shows a lower median, we’ll re-run the model cost scenario (the attached XLS has a sensitivity tab).

Concrete pilot framing (proposal)
- Scope: 6-week closed pilot scoped to 1 high-volume transactional flow (end-to-end integration with one environment).
- Success metrics: unit cost per transaction <= target band you set; latency P95 < 350ms; cache hit rate > 30% within 2 weeks.
- Runbook: week 0 integration + test traffic, weeks 1–4 observe & tune batching/cache settings, week 5 optimization pass + SLO validation, week 6 readout + decision gate.

Example math (illustrative)
- Baseline: 200k transactions * 550 tokens = 110M tokens/month.
- If batching/cache reduce tokens by 25% -> 82.5M tokens.
- At an effective $/1k-token of $2.00 (pilot pricing example) -> monthly cost = 82.5k * $2.00 = $165k (this is a raw example; our actual proposal applies committed discounts and different model tiers to get the number closer to your budget).
- Key point: without batching/cache the raw spend is much higher; the levers are what make an affordable pilot possible.

Security snippet and SOC2
- Attaching a one-page security snippet with retention and key management notes (CardinalPay_security_snippet.pdf). Our SOC2 summary is publicly available at: https://redwood.com/security/soc2-brief.pdf — we can also provide an in-depth package upon NDA.

Next steps (for clarity)
1) If you can confirm the $12k/month pilot band we’ll prepare a short SOW and strip-down invoice for procurement.
2) I’ll share a docs link with the integration checklist and a limited-access sandbox.
3) Wed 10am PT technical kickoff (I’ll send invite if that works).

I’ve looped Marissa (solutions) and Karthik (inference optimizations) so they can join the kickoff and surface any operational constraints up front.

Best,
Rachel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
